_note: What code must decide for each planted scenario in demo/generate.py (SCENARIOS), from the policy in packages/ioc-report/src/ioc_report/rules.py.

`rules`: the explaining rules of an explained case, or the keeping rules of a review case ('unexplained' when none holds and an item is left unexplained). `explained_by`: every rule that explains one of the case's contacts or flows, whatever the disposition.

Revised after the first run, for K3 only: K3 holds when the published triage stream has an episode on the flagged destination itself. Triage hashes an unnamed contact on a routed address under its ASN, so the beacon's episodes cannot count (no K3). Triage's relationship family raises an episode on a new rare name (the tunnel visitor's bore.pub, the lure domain), and its persistence family raises one every day on a rare name a host uses daily (the tunnel client's bore.pub), so those cases also carry K3. The tunnel client's contacts are still explained by E5.

_small_world_optional._note: Rules the small world (--hosts-per-profile) may or may not raise; the full world requires them. The tunnel visitor's K3 rests on a relationship episode whose strength is a peer percentile: 98.48 among 120 office hosts on 2026-11-23 (the world ending 2026-11-24), just past the 97.5 tail, and below it among the small world's 48. Its disposition, K1 and K2 are still required.
